principles: A producer guard must refuse exactly the set of inputs its consumer would accept as duplicates - predicate parity, not predicate approximation.
Never destroy standing evidence: a refusal that explains the standing quorum beats a write that invalidates it.
Recovery paths for append-only committed metadata must be official commands with dry-run defaults and backups, never manual file surgery.
Smallest change that closes the incident class; structural migrations (id schemes) only with their own story and migration plan.
drivers: The B-bf52 incident: a redundant re-submit after git merge main silently dropped assurance from full-3x2 to ordinary review, with no recovery command (manual jsonl surgery, commit 255eefd289).
The floor's drift-accept predicate (eventsWithStoryFilesHashDowngrade, review-escalation.ts:948-969) is authoritative and explicitly excluded from change in this story.
Deterministic runIds (<storyId>-q-rN) and story+host-derived session/key identities are load-bearing for existing verdict history and smoke assertions - migration cost is real.

options.name: guard-predicate-alignment-plus-prune
pros: Closes the poisoning path at the producer with a few-line predicate change mirroring the floor exactly
Refusal message teaches the operator the standing quorum is still valid (encodes the write-once-per-material rule into the tool)
quorum_prune formalizes the proven B-bf52 recovery (keep=newest-material matches commit 255eefd289) for already-poisoned stories
No id-scheme migration, no verdict-history rewrite, existing smoke assertions stay valid
cons: Guard must track the floor predicate in lockstep (documented in the guard comment; empty-hash corner deliberately mirrored per OQ-1 resolution)
quorum_prune rewrites an append-only committed file (contained by dry-run default, backup, pre-dirty refusal)

options.name: material-scoped-runIds
pros: Structurally removes cross-material runId collisions forever
No guard/floor predicate coupling to maintain
cons: Requires migrating existing stories' verdict history and every -q-rN smoke/format assertion
Redundant resubmits become silently accepted extra rounds (drift-accepted old rounds + new rounds double-count) instead of a teaching refusal
Does not help already-poisoned stories at all (still needs a prune path)

options.name: supersede-events
pros: Keeps the append-only log append-only during recovery
Full audit trail of what superseded what
cons: Every verdict consumer (floor, escalation, summaries, offline verifier) must learn supersede semantics - a trust-model change far larger than the incident class
Still needs the producer guard anyway to stop new poisonings; supersede alone only remediates

rationale: The incident class is fully closed by making the producer refuse exactly what the consumer drift-accepts, and the one real historical poisoning already validated the prune recovery shape (keep newest-material). The alternatives cost a migration or a trust-model change and still need the guard anyway.

preMortem.scenario: Floor later gains the EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH no-signal guard while the quorum guard keeps mirroring the old predicate
preMortem.trigger: A future story hardens eventsWithStoryFilesHashDowngrade per review-run-binding-race.md
preMortem.consequence: Guard refuses a resubmit the floor would no longer drift-accept - over-blocking; the guard comment names this lockstep dependency so that story updates both, and the refusal message points at review_escalation_status which would reveal the mismatch.
preMortem.mitigation: The guard comment names the lockstep dependency on eventsWithStoryFilesHashDowngrade and the refusal message points at review_escalation_status, so any future floor hardening story finds and updates both predicates together.

preMortem.scenario: quorum_prune removes the wrong verdict set on a story where the newest-material set is itself the erroneous one
preMortem.trigger: Operator poisoned a quorum by resubmitting at an OLD checkout (newest event is not the wanted one)
preMortem.consequence: Floor stays broken until re-pruned; contained by dry-run default listing both sets with digests before apply, the keep=oldest-material selector, and the timestamped backup enabling restore.
preMortem.mitigation: dryRun defaults on and lists both verdict sets with material digests before any mutation; keep=oldest-material selector covers the inverted case; a timestamped backup enables full restore.

preMortem.scenario: Legacy verdict events without a storyFilesHash field meet the new guard
preMortem.trigger: Old stories created before storyFilesHash was written into verdicts run quorum_submit again
preMortem.consequence: Guard must not fabricate a collision from a blank field; blank storyFilesHash is treated as no-signal (no drift-accept claim), preserving pre-fix behavior for legacy history - covered by CHK-002:edge:0.
preMortem.mitigation: The guard treats a blank/absent storyFilesHash field as no-signal (no drift-accept claim), preserving pre-fix behavior for legacy verdict history; locked by CHK-002:edge:0.

preMortem.scenario: quorum_prune apply races a concurrent lattice command writing process-events.jsonl
preMortem.trigger: Another host appends a verdict between prune's read and rewrite
preMortem.consequence: Lost append or corrupted jsonl; contained by running through the same lifecycle-metadata transaction machinery as quorum_submit (pre-dirty refusal + exact-append verification + rollback), which refuses when the tree or file moved.
preMortem.mitigation: quorum_prune runs through the same lifecycle-metadata transaction machinery as quorum_submit (pre-dirty refusal, exact-content verification, rollback on failure), refusing whenever the tree or the events file moved underneath it.
